quests.title: Emergency Power
quests.description: Bring two D-cell batteries to Imani so the rooftop repeater can survive the night.

quests.title: The Roof Clinic
quests.description: Deliver a field medkit to Doctor Park before the rooftop clinic runs dry.

quests.title: Thin the Mist
quests.description: Destroy three creatures at street level so Mateo can reopen a supply route.

quests.title: Voices on the Roofs
quests.description: Meet five rooftop survivors and carry their names back to Grace.

quests.title: One More Crossing
quests.description: Bring Tomas a portable ladder for a new route between isolated roofs.

quests.title: Signal Fire
quests.description: Find an emergency flare for Malik's rescue signal.

quests.title: Supper for Two
quests.description: Bring two cans of food for Nia and her missing brother.

greetings.low: Stop there. I remember how you spoke to people. Say what you need and keep your hands where I can see them.
greetings.neutral: You made it above the mist. Good. I am Imani. Everything on these roofs has a name, an owner, and a cost.
greetings.high: There you are. I kept the useful stock aside; people I trust should not have to bargain with panic.

progress.text: The repeater dies whenever the sun drops. Without it, the roofs become ten separate islands.
Word is moving again. The roofs know someone is crossing the gaps and coming back alive.
We are starting to look like a settlement instead of a collection of last mistakes.

topics.text: Keeping a ledger now is how people learn to trust tomorrow.
topics.response: Exactly. I count tins and rounds, but what I am really counting is promises. A roof survives when both totals balance.

topics.text: Your prices are steep for supplies people need.
topics.response: The price stops one frightened person from taking every bandage. Bring me a fairer system that still works at midnight, and I will use it.

topics.text: What did you see when the breach opened?
topics.response: A second skyline behind the first. Then the mist folded the street in half. I stopped looking when something looked back.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: Emergency Power] I can bring two D-cell batteries.
dialogue.quest_offer: Take this seriously. Two sealed D-cells will keep the emergency repeater alive through one night. Bring them to me intact.
dialogue.quest_active: The repeater is still coughing static. I need two D-cell batteries, not promises.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: I have the two batteries for the repeater.
dialogue.quest_complete: Good. Tonight every roof will hear the warning if the things in the mist start climbing. Take the scrip; you earned more than that.

greetings.low: If you are here to shout, do it away from my patients.
greetings.neutral: I am Doctor Park. I have a tarp, rainwater, and six people pretending their wounds are clean.
greetings.high: I am glad it is you. Sit for ten seconds and let me see whether the mist has left anything under your skin.

progress.text: The first symptom is exhaustion. The second is insisting the whispering is only wind.
Fewer patients are arriving. I cannot decide whether that is good news.
We have a real clinic now. Small, cold, and real.

topics.text: Tell me who needs help first.
topics.response: The quiet ones. Panic is loud enough to triage itself. Check the person who says they are fine and cannot stop shaking.

topics.text: Are the people touched by the mist still human?
topics.response: That is a moral question wearing a medical coat. Their blood changes. Their memories do not, at least not immediately.

topics.text: You cannot save everyone. Stop wasting supplies.
topics.response: I choose who can be saved every hour. You do not get to make that sound easy for me.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: The Roof Clinic] What supplies are you missing?
dialogue.quest_offer: A proper field medkit. One. There is a child with glass near an artery, and my clean gauze is almost gone.
dialogue.quest_active: I can hold the bleeding for now. Bring one field medkit before 'for now' becomes an obituary.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: Here is the field medkit. Use it on the child.
dialogue.quest_complete: Set it here. Good. You bought someone a future; do not let anyone reduce that to inventory.

greetings.low: Great. The rooftop hero. Try not to solve me while you are here.
greetings.neutral: Mateo. I used to deliver noodles in eleven minutes. Now I deliver bad news across rooftops.
greetings.high: My favorite impossible delivery. Tell me you found another way through.

progress.text: The service alley below is blocked by three of those pale crawlers. They barely see, but they hear everything.
The route map is growing. I mark safe crossings in blue and missing people in red.
Yesterday this map was mostly red. You are changing the color of the city.

topics.text: Being afraid and running messages anyway is courage.
topics.response: That sounds better than 'too scared to stay still.' I will borrow your version.

topics.text: Which street route still works?
topics.response: Cut through the Galleria lobby, stay off the tile near the eggs, then take the loading corridor north. Never sprint blind in fog.

topics.text: If you were faster, those people would already have supplies.
topics.response: Fast does not help when the road grows teeth. You want the route sooner, walk it yourself.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: Thin the Mist] I can clear your service route.
dialogue.quest_offer: Drop three mist creatures near the service alley. Any three. Once the noise stops, I can move medicine between the north roofs.
dialogue.quest_active: The route stays closed until three of them are down. Do not chase them deeper than you can see.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: The service route is clear. Three creatures are down.
dialogue.quest_complete: Then people eat tonight. Here, take my route money. I can earn more once the wheels turn again.

greetings.low: Names matter. Manners do too, though the end of the world has made both unfashionable.
greetings.neutral: Grace Holloway. I kept the Northbank library for thirty-eight years. Now I keep the names of the living.
greetings.high: Come here, dear. I saved a dry chair and one story that does not end in fog.

progress.text: People vanish twice: once in the mist, and once when nobody remembers their name.
Your list has become a web. People who thought they were alone can hear one another.
The archive has more living names than dead ones today. That is victory enough.

topics.text: Tell me one name I should remember.
topics.response: Daniel Holloway. My husband. He hated heights, loved apricot jam, and went downstairs to hold the lobby door. Remember all of it.

topics.text: Did the old books mention anything like the breach?
topics.response: Not facts. Patterns. Doors opened by pride, bargains mistaken for experiments, and fog that behaves like a guest invited inside.

topics.text: Lists will not keep anyone alive.
topics.response: No. People keep people alive. A list reminds us who we are doing it for.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: Voices on the Roofs] Whose names are missing?
dialogue.quest_offer: Meet five survivors on these roofs. Look at them when they speak. Bring their names back so no island believes it is alone.
dialogue.quest_active: Five living names. Not descriptions, not headcounts. Speak to them.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: I have met five rooftop survivors. I remember their names.
dialogue.quest_complete: Then write them here. The city is smaller now, in the best possible way.

greetings.low: Do not touch the dial. Last person who did erased six hours of signal hunting.
greetings.neutral: I am Jun. That clicking is not interference. Interference does not count backward in prime numbers.
greetings.high: Perfect timing. The voice came back, and I need someone who will believe me before it stops.

progress.text: Every night at 02:13, someone broadcasts from below the Galleria. The message is only breathing and coordinates.
The repeater gave me a second bearing. The signal moves without using the streets.
I heard our own call sign answer from the other side of the breach, twelve seconds before I transmitted it.

topics.text: I believe you heard something. Save the recording.
topics.response: Already copied three times. Thank you for saying 'something.' Adults keep deciding what it is before they listen.

topics.text: Give me the frequency and coordinates.
topics.response: Fourteen point zero seven megahertz. The coordinates resolve beneath the fountain, but the mall plans show no basement there.

topics.text: You are a kid playing with a broken radio.
topics.response: And you are an adult standing in an invasion pretending age is evidence. We are both disappointed.

greetings.low: Mum said not to trust people who make themselves feel tall by talking down to children.
greetings.neutral: I am Nia. I can see three roofs from here and the monsters cannot see me if I stay behind the water tank.
greetings.high: You came back! I kept watch like you said. Two crawlers went east and one climbed a bus, then fell off.

progress.text: My brother Leon is on another roof. He has a red coat. If you see red moving in the fog, check before you shoot.
Grace put Leon's name in her book. That means other people are looking too.
We made signal flags from hotel sheets. Mine means safe, danger, and bring chocolate.

topics.text: Your observations help everyone. Keep using cover.
topics.response: I write times too. Grown-ups say 'a while ago,' but a while is useless when you are counting monsters.

topics.text: Tell me exactly where you last saw Leon.
topics.response: West of the hotel, near the roof with the green chairs. He flashed a mirror twice before the fog got thick.

topics.text: You should hide and leave scouting to adults.
topics.response: Adults did not notice the eggs until I showed them. I will hide when hiding is the useful job.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: Supper for Two] Do you and Leon have food?
dialogue.quest_offer: I saved my apple, but Leon hates apples. Two cans would be enough if he gets back tonight. I can pay; I found scrip in the laundry room.
dialogue.quest_active: Two cans. One for me and one for Leon. I am not eating his, even if he is late.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: I brought two cans, one for each of you.
dialogue.quest_complete: Thank you. I knew he would need dinner when he comes back. That is not pretending. That is planning.

greetings.low: You step over my tools again, you can fix your own elevator.
greetings.neutral: Varga. Superintendent. The city forgot buildings are machines, so the machines chose today to complain.
greetings.high: Good hands are rare. Yours keep returning with the same number of fingers, which is promising.

progress.text: Elevators still run because I bypassed every safety rule written after 1978.
New crossings change the load on old roofs. Walk near beams, not skylights.
Give me a week and I can turn these roofs into one ugly, defensible neighborhood.

topics.text: The lifts are keeping people alive. Good work.
topics.response: Machines respond to respect. People too, occasionally. Keep the doors clear and listen for the second clunk.

topics.text: Where should the next bridge go?
topics.response: Depot to Galleria. Short span, strong parapets, and it joins food to shelter. I marked the brackets in orange.

topics.text: Just force every elevator door. We do not have time for caution.
topics.response: Force the wrong interlock and the car becomes a coffin with buttons. Caution is time you get to use later.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: One More Crossing] What do you need for the depot bridge?
dialogue.quest_offer: A portable steel ladder. I will brace it and bolt the ends. Bring one, and two isolated roofs become neighbors.
dialogue.quest_active: One portable ladder. Do not bring rope and optimism; neither has a load rating.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: I have a portable ladder for the crossing.
dialogue.quest_complete: Straight rails, sound locks. This will hold. Stand back while I make it permanent.

greetings.low: If you came to blame a scientist, take a number. I am busy measuring the apocalypse.
greetings.neutral: Asha Singh, Breach Dynamics. Before you ask: yes, our experiment opened it. No, it was not supposed to have weather.
greetings.high: I need your field observations. You notice what instruments miss, and you do not faint when the answer moves.

progress.text: The mist is not vapor. It is a boundary condition pretending to be weather.
Every cleared route changes its flow. Something on the other side may be learning our map.
I can model a way to narrow the breach. Closing it is still a word, not a plan.

topics.text: Tell people the whole truth, even if they hate you for it.
topics.response: I released the logs. I left my name on them. Accountability will not close the breach, but secrecy helped open it.

topics.text: What does your model predict next?
topics.response: A pressure pulse after midnight. The fog rises, electronics fail, and large organisms move toward concentrated heat.

topics.text: Everyone below is there because of you.
topics.response: Some of them are. I carry that arithmetic every second. If punishment fixes the sky, tell me where to stand.

greetings.low: I need clear answers and clear exits. If you cannot offer either, move.
greetings.neutral: Captain Reed. We held the west stairwell until the fog started coming up through concrete.
greetings.high: Good to see you upright. The rescue teams listen when I say your route is safe.

progress.text: I have people flashing mirrors from the west roofs. We need a signal they can see through the haze.
We pulled seven people across your routes. One had been trapped since the first night.
The crews have sectors now. We are responding instead of reacting.

topics.text: Your crew held longer than anyone had a right to expect.
topics.response: They held because someone behind them needed another minute. That is the whole job, stripped of uniforms and speeches.

topics.text: Does fire keep the mist creatures away?
topics.response: Light draws some and drives off others. Heat definitely changes the fog. Never light a flame without knowing both exits.

topics.text: Your chain of command is gone. Stop giving orders.
topics.response: The badge is gone. The responsibility is not. You are free to ignore me; the fire is free to ignore you too.

dialogue.quest_prompt: [Quest: Signal Fire] What can reach the west roofs?
dialogue.quest_offer: An emergency flare. One bright burn from this height tells the trapped teams where our safe stairwell is.
dialogue.quest_active: Bring one emergency flare. A torch is too dim, and gunfire sends the wrong message.
dialogue.quest_turn_in: I found an emergency flare for your signal.
dialogue.quest_complete: That will do. At dusk we fire it east, then west. Anyone still watching gets a direction home.

greetings.low: You have influence and no discipline. That combination buried the old city faster than the mist did.
greetings.neutral: Evelyn Ward. I used to coordinate emergency policy. Nobody laughs at the word 'coordination' anymore.
greetings.high: I have been waiting for you. People report what they fear to officials; they tell you what they actually saw.

progress.text: Every roof is inventing its own law. By morning, that becomes ten kinds of justice and no shared rescue plan.
Imani has supply numbers, Grace has names, and Reed has routes. We can build one plan from all three.
The roof council meets at sunset. For the first time, every connected building is sending someone.

topics.text: A council should include the children and isolated roofs too.
topics.response: Agreed. Survival does not suspend representation; it makes exclusion lethal. Nia gets a seat if she wants one.

topics.text: What decision cannot wait until morning?
topics.response: Whether to concentrate everyone at the Galleria or keep distributed shelters. One fire favors separation. One coordinated attack favors the mall.

topics.text: Politics caused this. We do not need another official.
topics.response: The experiment caused this. Politics decides who gets the last respirator. Refusing to name that choice does not make it disappear.
